title: Deleting auxiliary boundary from a tame Kummer cover
statement:
Let $Y$ be a Noetherian regular scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme], [pqf-def-locnoeth] with a normal crossings divisor $\overline D$, and let $q:V\to Y$ be a finite normal generically free $G$-quotient for a finite group $G$. The quotient has invariant structure sheaf and geometric fibres the orbits. Suppose that, with the inverse-image divisorial log structures, $(V,q^{-1}\overline D)\to(Y,\overline D)$ is a Kummer etale $G$-cover, and is tame. Kummer etale means etale locally a strict base change of an injective fs monoid chart map with every target element having a positive multiple in the image and with finite group-completion cokernel of order invertible locally. Let $D\subseteq\overline D$ be a reduced union of irreducible components, and suppose $q$ is etale over $Y\setminus D$. Then $(V,q^{-1}D)\to(Y,D)$, with reduced boundaries and divisorial log structures, is a Kummer etale $G$-cover; $(V,q^{-1}D)$ is fs log regular and the action on it is very tame. In particular the auxiliary components in $\overline D\setminus D$ can be deleted. Very tame means invertible inertia order and trivial inertia action on characteristic monoids and on strict local log strata [def-trf-fs-log-blowup].

More generally Kummer etale G-covers are stable under arbitrary base change in fs log schemes. A Kummer etale cover of a locally Noetherian fs log regular scheme is fs log regular, its inertia action is very tame, and its restriction over an open on which the base has trivial log structure is an ordinary finite etale G-cover. In a birational saturated log blowup base change, the pulled-back cover is the normalization of the modified base in the original generic cover. For such a Kummer etale $G$-cover, the underlying finite scheme morphism is etale on the locus with trivial geometric inertia. All assertions apply componentwise to a finite disjoint union. Here a normal crossings divisor is a reduced effective Cartier divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal] which etale locally at every point is cut out by a product of distinct members of a regular system of parameters; its global irreducible components may self-intersect, and a strict normal crossings divisor [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary] is the special case with regular components.

source.place: VIII 5.3.8, printed p.125, last paragraph, using the variant of Abhyankar in IX Proposition 2.1, printed p.133; VI 1.8, 2.3 and 3.1--3.2, printed pp.70--74. Stability under fs base change is VI 2.1--2.3, printed pp.71--73; the normalization identification is VIII 5.3.8--5.3.10.

proof.text: Work etale locally at a point of $Y$, where the normal crossings divisor and its selected union $D$ are strict. The regular-boundary chart theorem gives a chart $P=\mathbf N^r$, $e_i\mapsto t_i$, for the canonical divisorial structure of $(Y,D)$, and proves it fs log regular. Apply the tame-inertia root normal form to $q$ with this smaller boundary. Its hypotheses hold: $V$ is normal and finite over the Noetherian $Y$, its geometric fibres are quotient orbits, the given action is tame and generically free, and $q$ is etale on $Y\setminus D$. Thus on pointed etale neighbourhoods the underlying ring is $B^K$ for $B=A[x_i]/(x_i^n-t_i)$, with $n$ invertible locally. The normal form uses inertia, so no invertibility of $|G|$ is inferred. This applies to each local branch even when a global component of the boundary self-intersects.

source.place: VIII 5.3.8, p.125, last paragraph; IX 2.1, pp.133--134

proof.text: Put $P=\mathbf N^r$ and $L=\{b/n\in(1/n)\mathbf Z^r:\sum k_i b_i=0\pmod n\ (k\in K)\}$, $Q=L\cap(1/n)\mathbf N^r$. The invariant-monoid algebra theorem identifies $B^K=A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q]$, with $P\hookrightarrow Q$ injective Kummer and finite group cokernel killed by $n$. Construct the associated log structure from $Q$; the toric comparison theorem gives the actual log morphism with this chart and isomorphic scheme comparison. The invertible-Kummer chart theorem now proves log regularity. A chart monomial becomes a unit precisely off the inverse image of $D$: its $n$th power is a product of the $t_i$, and the generators of $P$ are among these monomials. The log-regular divisorial theorem therefore identifies this log sheaf, as a subsheaf of functions, with $\mathcal O_V\cap j_*\mathcal O_{V\setminus q^{-1}D}^{\times}$. Consequently the local sheaves and log maps agree on overlaps; they are the canonical smaller divisorial structures. This proves the Kummer etale chart assertion and fs log regularity globally.

The original action preserves $q^{-1}D$, so acts on the constructed divisorial log structure. At the selected strict-local point the root normal form identifies inertia with $(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)^r/K$. Finite character-annihilator duality identifies this quotient with $\operatorname{Hom}(L/\mathbf Z^r,\mu_n)$, compatibly with $z^q\mapsto\chi_q z^q$. Hence its action is exactly the standard Kummer deck action. The standard-model theorem says that the canonical fs diagonal is the disjoint union of copies indexed by these characters. Inducing from the stabilizer to $G$ accounts for all the strict-local components of the finite cover, giving $\coprod_G V\simeq V\times_Y^{\rm fs}V$. Thus the smaller-boundary morphism is a $G$-cover, not merely a Kummer etale morphism. The standard comparison also verifies the original $G$-action: on the dense complement it is the given deck action, and on the normal affine model two maps agreeing on that dense open agree on functions.

For any finite Kummer etale $G$-cover of a locally Noetherian fs log regular base, apply the invertible-Kummer chart theorem to obtain log regularity of the source. Strict-locally the standard-model theorem writes a component as $\operatorname{Spec}B$, $B=A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q]$, with sharp $P,Q$ and inertia the character deck group. Let $I=(z^p:p\ne0)A$ and $J=(z^q:q\ne0)B$. There is a canonical isomorphism $B/J=A/I$: quotienting the monoid algebra by all its nonconstant monomials leaves $\mathbf Z$, and tensoring gives exactly this quotient of $A$. Every character fixes $A$ and scales monomials by units, so fixes $Q$ modulo units and acts identically on $B/J$. Its order divides a power of the invertible chart exponent, hence is invertible. These three computations are exactly very tameness on every strict-local stratum. They apply in particular to the smaller-boundary cover of Steps 1--3; no assertion that its underlying source scheme is regular is needed.

For arbitrary fs base change $Y'\to Y$ take, etale locally, the chart $P\to Q$ of the cover given by Kummer etaleness, and by the chart-existence clause of the saturated-pushout algebra theorem a chart $R$ of $Y'$ with a compatible map $P\to R$. The saturated-pushout algebra theorem realizes the fs product by $S=(Q\oplus_P R)^{\rm int,sat}$. Its assertions give an injective Kummer map $R\to S$ with the same finite group cokernel killed by an integer invertible on the new base. The comparison is the base change of the old etale chart comparison, hence etale by ordinary etale base change. The theorem's finite surjective comparison to the ordinary scheme product, followed by the ordinary base change of the finite cover, proves finiteness and surjectivity. The fs product universal property pulls back the isomorphism $\coprod_G V\simeq V\times_Y^{\rm fs}V$ to $\coprod_G V'\simeq V'\times_{Y'}^{\rm fs}V'$, preserving the given action and all compositions. These chart constructions glue by their universal property. Thus this is stability of $G$-covers for arbitrary fs bases, including non-Noetherian bases; local Noetherianity is used only for the separate regularity assertion.

On a trivial-log open, injectivity and the Kummer condition force the source characteristic monoid to be zero: a positive multiple of each element is zero and a sharp saturated monoid has no nonzero torsion. In the sharp strict-local standard model this is $P=Q=0$, so every component is the identity. The cover there is therefore ordinary finite etale, with its $G$-torsor action. For the general trivial-inertia assertion, take an affine base open and its finite, $G$-stable affine inverse image $\operatorname{Spec}R$. The standard-model invariant equalities, applied to each strict-local component and its induced $G$-action, identify the base ring with $R^G$. At a point with trivial geometric inertia the inertia subgroup $I$ in the finite-group invariants lemma is $1$: its condition is precisely preservation of the prime and identity on its residue field. Thus $R^I=R$, and that lemma gives etaleness on an open neighbourhood of the point in $\operatorname{Spec}R$. This proves etaleness on the entire trivial-inertia locus without a regularity assumption on the underlying source scheme.

source.place: Tag 0BST, lemma-inertia-invariants-etale; for the trivial-log standard models, ILO VI 2.2--2.3, pp.72--73

proof.text: Let $b:Y'\to Y$ now be a birational saturated log blowup of a locally Noetherian fs log regular base, and pull the finite Kummer cover back in fs log schemes. On each integral component the log-blowup theorem makes $Y'$ log regular and leaves the dense trivial-log open unchanged. Steps 4--5 give a finite log regular pullback $V'\to Y'$. By the divisorial-structure theorem $V'$ is normal and its trivial-log locus is dense. The Kummer condition identifies that locus with the inverse image of the base's trivial-log locus, and Step 6 identifies the cover there with the ordinary pulled-back finite etale generic cover. Each component therefore has the original generic field over the corresponding birationally modified base component. Apply finite-normal-cover recognition on these integral components: its affine ring is precisely the integral closure of the modified base ring in that field. The canonical identifications glue, proving that the fs pullback is the normalization in the original generic cover. Finiteness comes from Step 5, with no excellence hypothesis.

A finite disjoint union has precisely the component log sheaves and local rings. Its fs fibre products, normalizations, and the canonical $G$-diagonal are computed componentwise, allowing $G$ to permute components. All pointwise chart, stratum and inertia computations above consequently apply to it. Empty boundaries give the ordinary finite etale case; empty unions and length-zero log blowups give the corresponding empty or identity constructions.

proof_origin.place: VIII 5.3.8--5.3.10; IX Proposition 2.1; VI 1.8,2.2--2.3; X 1.8. Explicit local algebra supplied in the steps.
